Program Overview.A: SDI Manufacturing Certificate & Associate of Science: Roadmap Built from Tooling U-SME Mappings

Certificate: Courses 1-8, 4 credits each = 32 credit hours. Covers all 28 CMfgA-tab lessons (100% of SME's Certified Manufacturing Associate requirement) plus 17 CMfgT-tab lessons (Applied Math and Materials Science fundamentals) that extend naturally out of the CMfgA content. Certificate graduates are positioned to sit for the SME CMfgA exam. Associate of Science: Courses 1-17. The Associate uses all 8 Certificate courses as transfer credit (32 credits) and adds 9 more courses (Courses 9-17, 36 credits) covering the remaining CMfgT-tab lessons plus the 10 Tooling U Manual Machining lessons (Manual Milling and Engine Lathe Practicums). Associate of Science total: 68 credit hours. Combined, Courses 1-8 and 9-17 cover all 161 CMfgT-tab lessons, positioning Associate of Science graduates to sit for the SME CMfgT exam. General education credits are not included, see note below.

Path A: Enroll in the Certificate (Courses 1-8), complete it, sit for the SME CMfgA exam. Later, return and enroll in the Associate of Science: the 8 Certificate courses transfer in directly (no repeat coursework), complete Courses 9-17, then sit for the SME CMfgT exam. Path B: Enroll directly in the Associate of Science and complete all 17 courses in one continuous enrollment, sitting for the SME CMfgA exam after Course 8 and the SME CMfgT exam after Course 17.

Program Overview.A: Design notes: (1) The Certificate (Courses 1-8) covers all 28 CMfgA-tab lessons, meeting the full SME CMfgA requirement, plus 17 CMfgT-tab lessons (Courses 3 and 4) that extend naturally out of the CMfgA math and materials content. Certificate graduates are positioned to sit for the SME CMfgA exam. (2) The Associate of Science (Courses 1-17) expands on the Certificate: Courses 1-8 transfer in directly as the first 32 credits, and Courses 9-17 add the remaining 123 CMfgT-tab lessons plus the 10 Manual Machining lessons (36 more credits, 68 total). Combined, Courses 1-17 cover all 161 CMfgT-tab lessons, positioning Associate of Science graduates to sit for the SME CMfgT exam. (3) The 10 Tooling U "Manual Machining" lessons (Manual Mill/Engine Lathe Basics through Taper Turning), which are not on either the CMfgA or CMfgT tab, sit in Associate of Science Courses 11 and 12 rather than in the Certificate. This is a deliberate cost decision: the mill and lathe tooling and equipment costs those two courses require are supportable at the Associate-level tuition margin, not the Certificate-level tuition margin. (4) A student who completes only the Certificate is not charged again for Courses 1-8 if they return for the Associate of Science; those credits transfer in directly. (5) The 68-credit Associate of Science technical core does not include general education coursework (composition, college math, social science, etc.). SDI's standard gen-ed course set would need to be layered on top to reach a full Associate of Science credit total; that catalog was not part of the materials provided, so no gen-ed courses or credits are estimated here. (6) This workbook reflects one possible sequencing of the CMfgA and CMfgT lesson sets into 4-credit course blocks; course titles, groupings, and week-by-week placement are a starting point for SDI's curriculum team to revise before this program design is finalized.
